# Recent Dispatches Summary

**Headline:** Add a `dispatches` filter axis to the Herdr worklist, bound to `f d`, that projects the local rolling downtime dispatch log into up to 20 deduplicated, newest-first work-item rows so operators can see what auto-dispatched work was done now that completing dispatches are auto-closed.

## Problem Statement

The downtime dispatcher now auto-closes panes whose dispatched work reached a clean terminal state, so completed work disappears from the active worklist without a durable, browsable trace. Operators currently have no in-plugin way to answer "what did the dispatcher do recently?" — they must open `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` (raw JSONL) or a separate project. A dedicated recent-dispatches view restores visibility of auto-completed work without re-opening it as active.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** reviewing overnight or downtime activity — wants to confirm the dispatcher did useful work and spot items that need attention.
- **On-call engineer** investigating a bad dispatch — wants the recently dispatched items and their outcomes at a glance.
- **Agent maintainer** tuning dispatch selection — wants a quick list of recent picks without parsing the log by hand.

**User Stories:**

- "As an operator, I want to press `f d` in the Herdr worklist and see the 20 most recent work items the dispatcher touched, so that I can see what work was done after auto-close."
- "As an on-call engineer, I want each row to show whether the dispatch finished cleanly or requires attention, so that I can triage without reading the raw log."
- "As a producer, I want a recent-dispatch row for an item that is now closed or deleted to still show its id and title, so that completed work does not vanish."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing `f` then `d` in the Herdr worklist activates a **recent dispatches** filter view. It follows the existing single filter-slot replace semantics: activating it clears any active stage/priority filter, and activating a stage/priority filter (or `f s s` / `f p s` / bare `/wl`) clears it. The list header renders a dispatches filter label (e.g. `(filtered: dispatches)`).
- The view lists **up to the 20 most recently dispatched work items**, newest first, read from `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`. Rows are **deduplicated by work item id** (one row per item); ordering and displayed metadata use that item's most recent log entry.
- Each row displays at least the **work item id** and a **title** taken from the log (not from `wl list`), so items that are now closed/deleted still appear. Where the log carries them, the row also shows the dispatch **kind** (intake/plan/audit/implement) and the latest pane-close **outcome** (e.g. `closed-as-plan-complete`, `requires-attention`).
- The dispatches view is read-only and derived from the log only: it does not mutate the log or work items, does not change the default browse list or the existing stage/priority filters, and yields a header showing `N item(s)` for the number actually found (≤ 20).
- Selecting a row (Enter) opens the detail view. When the item still exists in `wl`, details are fetched fresh by id; when it does not, the view falls back to the log-derived metadata and does **not** crash or show a blank item.
- **Fail-safe:** a missing, unreadable, empty, or malformed log yields an empty dispatches list (0 items) with no crash and no error banner, reusing the existing fail-safe log-reader contract. The view participates in the normal auto-refresh cadence so a newly appended log entry appears on the next refresh.
- New unit and integration tests cover: log→row projection (dedup by id, newest-first ordering, 20-row cap, kind/outcome mapping, missing title, malformed lines), the empty/missing-log fail-safe path, chord recognition (`f d` and `/wl dispatches`), the header filter label, the filter replace/clear semantics, and the detail fallback for an item absent from `wl`.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`packages/herdr/README.md` documents the `f d` chord and view semantics; `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` cross-references the new view).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Source of truth is the local log:** `<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`, read via the existing fail-safe `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)`. The log is per-worklog-root and bounded to the most recent `DOWNTIME_LOG_MAX_ENTRIES` (100) entries, so 20 recent items normally fall inside the retained window.
- **No machine-wide aggregation** in this view — cross-project aggregation belongs to the separate `/skill:dispatch-logs` effort (WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40).
- **No new runtime dependencies.**
- **Display-only:** the view never writes the log, never mutates work items, and never spawns `wl` processes beyond the existing refresh/detail fetches.
- **Single filter slot:** dispatches, stage, and priority remain mutually exclusive (replace semantics), matching `WL-0MSKC8T46006999S`.
- **Fail-safe:** log read/parse failures must never crash the TUI or blank the list unexpectedly.

## Existing State

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` already provides the fail-safe, bounded reader `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)`, the `DOWNTIME_LOG_FILE` constant, and the `DowntimeLogEntry` shape. The log holds two row kinds: dispatch markers (`itemId`, `kind`, `dispatchedAt`, `title`, `stage`, optional `paneId`/`enrichment`) and pane-close lifecycle entries (`entryType: 'pane-close'`, `timestamp`, `itemId`, `itemTitle`, `kind`, `outcome`, `reason`, `reasonCode`).
- Filter axes live in `WorkItemListState` (`activeFilter`, `activePriorityFilter`, `_applyFilters`, `activeFilterLabel`), are dispatched by `dispatchChordCommand` from `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` chords, and are fetched through `fetchItemsForView`.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` defines the `f s *` stage and `f p *` priority chords; `f d` is currently free.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` fetches work items from `wl` (which omits closed items for stage filters), so a log-derived view cannot rely on `wl list` for its rows; `fetchItemDetails(id)` exists for single-item detail.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` wires refresh and view-command detection (`isWlViewCommand`) after chord dispatch.
- A separate Python `/skill:dispatch-logs` command (WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40, still in planning) generates a global 24-hour report across projects — complementary, not this view.

## Desired Change

Add a `dispatches` filter axis to the Herdr worklist, bound to `f d`, that projects the local rolling dispatch log into up to 20 synthetic work-item rows (deduplicated by id, newest first) rendered by the existing list and metadata panel, with best-effort detail fallback and fail-safe empty-state behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — add a projection helper (e.g. `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit)`) that reads via `readDowntimeLogEntries` and dedupes/orders/caps; or place the projection in a small new module.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — build synthetic `WorkItem` rows from log entries (id, title, stage, kind/outcome annotations), and reuse `fetchItemDetails` for the detail fallback.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — new `dispatches` axis: `applyFilter`/`_applyFilters` pass-through, `activeFilterLabel`, `fetchItemsForView` branch, `dispatchChordCommand` recognition of `/wl dispatches`, header label, detail-fallback handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` — add the `["f","d"]` chord → `/wl dispatches` entry.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — recognise the view command in `isWlViewCommand` so dispatch triggers an immediate refetch.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` — projection, fail-safe, chord, header, replace/clear, and detail-fallback tests.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — document the `f d` view and its semantics.

## Related Work

- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** (done) — Log all dispatches and auto-close all completed dispatch panes, except implement. Created the auto-close behaviour that makes completed work invisible and motivates this view.
- **WL-0MSGPI4AR000YOK8** (done) — Log herdr downtime dispatches (item comment + rolling `.worklog` log). Introduced the log this view reads.
- **WL-0MU4URK4H006OFCE** (done) — Extend dispatch log schema and add pane lifecycle monitor. Added the `pane-close` entries whose outcomes this view surfaces.
- **WL-0MUBVL251006JAQ0** (done) — Dispatcher log: selection path and pane id. Extended marker provenance fields.
- **WL-0MSKC8T46006999S** (done) — Herdr: filter by priority via `f p *` chords (stage filters become `f s *`). The precedent for filter-axis chords and replace semantics this view follows.
- **WL-0MSGTSPXK007POB1** (done) — Herdr worklist: show filter in header. The header filter-label mechanism this view reuses.
- **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7** (done) — Add key/chord to return to default browse view from stage-filtered list. Clear-filter behaviour the new axis must honour.
- **WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40** (plan_complete) — Dispatch-logs skill: global 24h dispatch report. Complementary cross-project reporting; shares the log-parsing concept but is a Python skill, not a Herdr view.
- **WL-0MU9J9MGB004NO8Q** (intake_complete) — Project root discovery and log aggregation (child of WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40). Relevant if a future machine-wide variant is requested.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Local-root scope (assumption).** The view reads only the current worklog root's log. Cross-project aggregation is deliberately out of scope and tracked by WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40. *Mitigation:* document the scope; a machine-wide variant is a follow-up work item.
- **Dedup/ordering semantics (assumption).** One row per work item, ordered by that item's most recent log entry; a later pane-close entry can reorder an item that was dispatched earlier. *Mitigation:* covered by explicit tests; revisit if the producer prefers "most recent dispatch time".
- **Detail fallback for closed/deleted items (assumption).** Log-derived rows may not resolve in `wl`; the detail view must degrade to the log metadata rather than blanking. *Mitigation:* best-effort fetch + fallback, explicitly tested.
- **Log rotation.** The log keeps only the most recent 100 entries, so a very busy period can push older "20th" candidates out of the file. *Mitigation:* accepted by design; document the 100-entry window.
- **Synthetic rows.** Rows are not live `wl` items, so fields such as priority/risk/effort/audit state are absent; the metadata panel may show `—`. *Mitigation:* show `—` gracefully; optionally mark rows as log-derived (used in AC3).
- **Refresh lag.** A very recent dispatch may not appear until the next auto-refresh tick. *Mitigation:* the view reuses the existing refresh cadence; acceptable for a summary.
- **Scope-creep risk.** Outcome annotations, click-to-open-from-detail, per-root filters, and a machine-wide view are candidates but out of scope here. *Mitigation:* record extra opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The session was auto-dispatched by the Herdr downtime worker with no operator present at interview time, so the questions below are recorded as **OPEN QUESTION**s with recommended defaults. The brief above adopts the recommended defaults so it is actionable; the producer may override any of them.

1. **OPEN QUESTION** — Q: What exactly counts as a "work item" row — the 20 most recent unique work items (one row per id) or the 20 most recent raw log entries (which would repeat an item when it is dispatched and later closed)? — Answer: *(awaiting producer)*. **Recommended:** deduplicate by work item id and order by the item's most recent log entry. Rationale: the request says "the 20 most recent work items", and repeating an id wastes scarce rows.
2. **OPEN QUESTION** — Q: Does "the dispatch log" mean only the current project's log, or a machine-wide aggregate across project roots? — Answer: *(awaiting producer)*. **Recommended:** the current worklog root only (`<worklog-root>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log`). Rationale: the Herdr plugin already resolves a single worklog root and the log is documented as per-root; machine-wide aggregation is the separate `/skill:dispatch-logs` effort (WL-0MTJQOZ0K007KD40).
3. **OPEN QUESTION** — Q: Should rows be selectable (Enter opens the detail view) or is a read-only summary sufficient? — Answer: *(awaiting producer)*. **Recommended:** selectable, with a best-effort detail fetch that falls back to log metadata for closed/deleted items. Rationale: it makes the view genuinely useful for investigation and reuses the existing detail machinery.
4. **OPEN QUESTION** — Q: Should each row surface the latest pane-close outcome and dispatch kind, or show only id/title/timestamp? — Answer: *(awaiting producer)*. **Recommended:** include kind and latest outcome when present. Rationale: distinguishing "closed cleanly" from "requires-attention" is the main reason to look at recent dispatches after auto-close.
5. **Assumption** — The view replaces the active stage/priority filter (single filter slot) rather than stacking with it, matching the existing `f p *` behaviour (WL-0MSKC8T46006999S). Source: existing implementation, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLX5OADB1TECIZV** – Testing: automation - create work item (completed)
- **WL-0MKRSO1KD1AN01Y9** – World Unique IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MKRRZ2DN032UHN5** – Issue syncing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `standups/2026_09_27.md` — matched: accessed, add, attention, auto, closing (+18 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: add, attention, auto, completed, dispatch (+16 more)
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: add, auto, closing, completed, dispatch (+16 more)

# Worklog recovery extension crashes pi on stale ExtensionContext after session replacement (`_notifyFn`)

## Headline

The Worklog recovery extension must stop crashing the pi process when its
captured `ExtensionContext` goes stale after a session replacement/reload; a
stale `ctx.ui` in the asynchronous retry-notification path must skip the
notification instead of throwing an uncaught exception that aborts headless
pi runs (e.g. the SorraAgents audit runner) with a spurious
`provider_error: Connection error.`

## Problem Statement

`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` captures
the event-handler `ctx` into a module-level notify closure (`_notifyFn`). That
closure is later invoked asynchronously from the retry loop
(`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`, driven by `triggerInvisibleContinue`).
After pi replaces or reloads the session, `ctx.ui.notify()` throws
`This extension ctx is stale after session replacement or reload …`. Because
the call originates in a timer/async callback
(`process.processTicksAndRejections`), pi does not catch it, the Node process
exits, and the calling consumer surfaces `provider_error: Connection error.`

## Users

- **As a pi extension maintainer**, I want the recovery extension to be
  resilient to session replacement/reload, so that an in-flight recovery
  notification cannot crash the whole pi process.
  - *As a maintainer, I want the stale-ctx notification path to be defensively
    guarded and covered by a regression test, so that future refactors cannot
    reintroduce the uncaught exception.*
- **As an operator running headless/audit pi sessions**, I want my long-running
  audit runs to complete rather than be aborted after ~12 minutes by an
  extension crash, so that reliability data is trustworthy.
  - *As an operator, I want the extension to degrade gracefully (skip the
    notification) when the session has been replaced, so that a cosmetic
    UI notification never has process-level impact.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The stale-ctx uncaught exception no longer occurs: the retry notification
   path (`_notifyRetryAttempt` → `_notifyFn`) never throws when the session
   ctx has been replaced/reloaded; the notification is skipped when the ctx is
   stale.
2. A regression test is added: invoking the retry notification path with an
   invalidated/stale ctx asserts no throw (and that the notification is
   skipped).
3. The Worklog extension test suite passes with the change; the full project
   test suite must pass with the new changes.
4. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries — specifically
   the recovery module header documenting the notify/ctx lifecycle.

## Constraints

- Do not change retry semantics otherwise (backoff, attempt counts, abort and
  session-generation guards, compaction-gate flow).
- Must not introduce npm dependencies beyond what the Worklog extension already
  uses.
- Follow existing Worklog extension conventions (module-level state pattern,
  `pi.on(...)` handlers, Vitest test layout under
  `lib/recovery/*.test.ts`).
- The guard must be defensive: completion/normal operation of the retry loop
  must not depend on UI notification succeeding.

## Existing State

- `register-recovery.ts` keeps module-level mutable state, including
  `_notifyFn` (line ~52), assigned from a captured handler `ctx` in the
  `agent_end` (line ~84) and `turn_end` (line ~88) handlers, and again in the
  `session_compact` handler (line ~212).
- `_notifyRetryAttempt` (line ~563) and other functions
  (`triggerCompactionContinue` ~462, `triggerCompactionGateRecovery`
  ~492/510/517) call `_notifyFn` asynchronously.
- `triggerInvisibleContinue` (line ~361) runs a `while (true)` retry loop,
  guarded by `interruptibleState.userAborted` and a
  `interruptibleState.sessionGeneration` comparison; it calls
  `_notifyRetryAttempt` (line ~408) after an interruptible sleep.
- `session_start` (line ~255) increments `interruptibleState.sessionGeneration`,
  resets retry/continuation state, but does **not** clear or re-bind
  `_notifyFn`.
- Existing recovery tests live alongside the source
  (`lib/recovery/*.test.ts`), e.g. `integration.test.ts`, `retry-loop.test.ts`,
  `compaction-gate.test.ts`, `session-compact.test.ts`, `retry-command.test.ts`.

## Desired Change

- `_notifyFn` must never throw after the ctx is invalidated. Re-bind/re-capture
  the notify function from the current handler ctx on each event that carries a
  ctx (and/or guard the call), so a stale ctx results in the notification being
  skipped rather than an uncaught exception.
- Consolidate the notify dispatch behind a single guarded helper (e.g. a
  `_safeNotify(message, level)` that wraps the captured `ctx.ui.notify` in a
  `try/catch`) so every call site (`_notifyRetryAttempt`,
  `triggerCompactionContinue`, `triggerCompactionGateRecovery`) shares the same
  stale-ctx protection.
- Consider clearing/re-capturing `_notifyFn` on `session_start` so a ctx from a
  replaced session is never retained, while a stale call still degrades to a
  no-op.
- Do not change retry semantics otherwise.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/register-recovery.ts` —
  `_notifyFn` capture (lines ~52, ~84, ~88, ~212) and call sites
  (`_notifyRetryAttempt` ~563, ~462, ~492/510/517); add guarded notify helper and
  stale-ctx regression coverage hooks.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/recovery/*.test.ts` — new regression
  test (a new `notify-safety.test.ts` or an addition to
  `retry-loop.test.ts`/`integration.test.ts`) asserting a stale/invalidated ctx
  does not throw from the retry notification path.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — Error Recovery Module section, if it
  documents the notify lifecycle (verify and update as needed).

## Related Work

- **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F** (SorraAgents) — corrected root-cause analysis and
  handoff that originated this item. The SorraAgents side will separately make
  its own `pi-client` extensions stale-ctx-safe and track its audit-runner
  change.
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** — Automatically recover from appropriate server
  errors (completed; the parent retry-loop context that introduced the recovery
  module and `_notifyFn`).
- Evidence: stack trace `_notifyFn (register-recovery.ts:71:41)` →
  `_notifyRetryAttempt (register-recovery.ts:549:5)` →
  `triggerInvisibleContinue (register-recovery.ts:391:7)` →
  `process.processTicksAndRejections`; SorraAgents audit debug log
  `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_SA-0MSRWAY9A005Q0CB.jsonl`
  (`context=parent`, `reason=provider_error`, `elapsed_seconds≈713`).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption**: the crash is confined to the `_notifyFn` closure; direct
  `ctx.ui.notify(...)` calls inside `pi.on` handlers receive a fresh ctx per
  event and are not affected. If other async paths retain a ctx, they must be
  audited too (scope-creep risk — record as linked work items rather than
  expanding this fix).
- **Risk (scope creep)**: hardening *all* captured ctx usage across the
  recovery module could balloon the change. **Mitigation**: fix the identified
  `_notifyFn` path and any trivially adjacent retained-ctx call sites; record
  broader stale-ctx hardening as separate work.
- **Risk**: a `try/catch` that silently swallows all notification errors could
  mask genuine UI/registration bugs. **Mitigation**: keep the catch narrow and
  documented (stale-ctx is expected after replacement); do not alter control
  flow on caught errors.
- **Risk**: tests that exercise `registerRecoveryModule` depend on pi's event
  API and monkey-patching; the regression test should target the notify helper /
  capture lifecycle in isolation where possible to stay deterministic.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions were required. The seed context is the detailed handoff
from **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F** (SorraAgents), which supplies the goal, root cause,
stack-trace evidence, desired change, acceptance criteria, key files, and
related work. Repo inspection confirmed the described `_notifyFn` capture and
call sites in `register-recovery.ts` and the absence of any guard. No open
questions remain; no producer decision is needed to proceed to planning.

- Q: "Are there any open questions or ambiguities that block planning the
  fix?" — Answer (agent research, 2026-09-28): None. The fix is scoped by AC1
  ("notification is skipped when the ctx is stale") and the desired change
  ("re-bind/re-capture … and/or guard the call"). Design latitude (re-capture
  vs. guard vs. both) is intentionally left to implementation and does not
  change the ACs. Evidence: `register-recovery.ts` lines ~52–88, ~212, ~408,
  ~563; existing recovery tests under `lib/recovery/`.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MQDR51JO0037ISJ** – Eliminate unsafe as any casts in shortcut dispatch (detail view and duck-typing) (completed)
- **WL-0MSNKWLER003EGE0** – Auto-recover from JSON parse errors in audit processing (completed)
- **WL-0MUKH3DVA00488U0** – [test-failure] tests/herdr/form-dialog.test.ts — 6 legacy expectations stale after shell-escape change (WL-0MU7KEX65004X0U9) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: acceptance, added, again, agent, analysis (+121 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: aborted, added, again, agent, appropriate (+103 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: added, again, agent, analysis, appropriate (+91 more)

# Downtime audits: prevent host-wide audit-slot / Local Proxy saturation from failing concurrent audits

**discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents worklog)

## Summary

On 2026-09-26 at least four downtime-dispatched audits were running concurrently on this
host, saturating both the shared Local Proxy and the audit runner's **host-wide** audit slot
(cheap-proxy mode forces `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1`). As a result the audit for
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` failed on **every** Pi call and was aborted with no verdict:

```
Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated:
no slot within 90s (waited 90.1s, 1 item(s) in queue)
```

Supporting observations at the time:

- A direct Local Proxy generation request (`POST http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1/chat/completions`,
  model `plan`) returned no response within 180s, while `/v1/models` answered immediately.
- Host load average was ~70.
- Concurrent audits: `SA-0MUFM54CA0010LVD` (SorraAgents), `SA-0MTTSWHQE0072N9J` (SorraAgents),
  `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` (ContextHub) alongside the aborted `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63`.
- The failure degraded every acceptance criterion to `partial` on infrastructure evidence
  (not a code assessment), so the audit produced no usable verdict.

## Existing coverage that did not prevent this

- **Per-instance active-audit detection** (`WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB`, tests `WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66`):
  the audit tier is skipped when a non-stale `kind=audit` dispatch marker in
  `<cwd>/.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` maps to an item still `in_progress`.
- **Proxy-slot gating** already exists in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
  (`slots_stale`, free-slot counts, local lease).

The observed concurrency spanned **multiple projects and possibly multiple herdr instances**,
and the audit runner's own host-wide semaphore/queue is a separate mechanism from the
dispatcher's per-project slot gate. The gap (per-instance vs host-wide coordination, and the
audit runner's 90s admission bound turning contention into an infra-partial verdict) is the
subject of this item.

## Desired change

1. **Host-wide audit serialisation (or deferral).** At most one audit-tier `/skill:audit` run
   should be actively executing per host — across herdr instances and projects — **or** the
   dispatcher must skip/defer audit dispatch while the audit runner's host-wide slot/queue is
   occupied or while the Local Proxy reports no free slots.
2. **Tolerate contention instead of failing.** When saturation is transient, the audit runner's
   admission wait should be sized so the run waits for a slot (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`) and/or the
   dispatch is retried later, rather than aborting with an infra-partial verdict. An audit must
   not be reported as unavailable merely because other audits are legitimately running.
3. **Regression test.** With a simulated occupied host-wide audit slot (or two dispatcher
   instances on one host), a second audit is not started; the candidate falls through to the
   next tier or is deferred.
4. **Observability.** Log a clear skip/defer reason (e.g. `audit-host-saturated`) that includes
   the number of concurrent audits and the audit-runner queue/slot state.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Audit dispatch is serialised host-wide (single active audit run per host) **or** audit
      dispatch is skipped/deferred when the host-wide audit slot or Local Proxy slots are
      unavailable, including across projects and herdr instances.
- [ ] A regression test proves a second concurrent audit is not started while one is active
      (simulated occupied slot / second instance), and that the candidate is deferred or falls
      through to another tier.
- [ ] Contention produces a clear `audit-host-saturated` (or equivalent) skip/defer log line
      with the concurrent-audit count and queue/slot state.
- [ ] Documentation of the host-wide coordination contract and its relationship to the existing
      per-instance active-audit detection and proxy-slot gating.

## Evidence

- Aborted audit log (SorraAgents):
  `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63_20260926T175346.log`
- SorraAgents work item with the full write-up and the producer Q&A: `SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63`.

## Related

- `WL-0MSI9WPNI0044RL8` — Audit dispatch tier
- `WL-0MT47BQAT00375VB` — Active-audit detection & audit-tier skip
- `WL-0MT47BMR7003ZQ66` — Active-audit single-flight tests
- `WL-0MSLIY8ZR004QUSY` — Downtime dispatcher triggers multiple identical sessions

## Notes

SorraAgents work items live in a separate worklog; this item is intentionally created in
ContextHub because the downtime dispatcher is implemented in `packages/herdr/`.

Create a new skill (proposed name: host-hygiene or perf-hygiene) that automates the manual machine-health analysis performed on 2026-09-27 (which resolved load 44 on 16 cores, CPU pressure 88.8%, a runaway 4.4 GB grep, orphaned audit_runners and stale vite servers).

## Purpose
A repeatable, safe diagnostic-and-remediation skill for hosts running many concurrent pi agent sessions and test suites. It must NEVER act autonomously without explicit producer approval.

## Required workflow (must be encoded in the skill)
1. **Evaluate** — collect performance metrics (load average, /proc/pressure/{cpu,memory,io}, free/swap, process & thread counts, per-command aggregate RSS, runnable count, stale devices) and render a before table with status symbols: low / warning / critical.
2. **Detail** — describe the primary pressures (which processes, which resources, attributable ancestry).
3. **Suggest** — propose concrete actions to relieve pressure (kills, pruning, pacing, session cleanup), each with target PIDs/paths and expected impact.
4. **Await producer input** — STOP. Present findings and wait for explicit approval. Do not kill, delete, or modify anything.
5. **Act on approval** — perform only the explicitly approved subset of actions.
6. **After table** — add an 'after' column to the original table showing current state, with per-metric priorities, and report residual/legitimate load.

## Constraints
- Read-only by default; destructive actions gated behind operator/producer approval.
- Must use wl for any work-item side effects and never edit .worklog data directly.
- Reusable across projects (global skill under skill/), with tests per skill-authoring conventions.
- Reference the analysis in WL-0MUJL0PTS009MC8F (debug-log rotation) and WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS (session close lifecycle) as related root causes.

## Acceptance criteria (draft)
- Skill file exists with the 6-step workflow and an explicit approval gate before any mutation.
- Diagnostic step reproduces the before/after tables (load, pressure, memory, swap, procs, threads, per-command RSS).
- Status symbols (low/warning/critical) defined with thresholds.
- Skill takes no destructive action in steps 1-4; step 5 only operates on an approved list.
- Tests cover threshold classification and the approval-gate refusal path.
- Documented in the skill index / discoverable via /skill invocation.

# Create the `pane-triage` skill — gated close of idle panes in the current herdr workspace

## Goal

As a producer running several herdr workspaces, I want a `/skill:pane-triage`
that reports every pane in the invoking workspace, splits them into idle vs
active, surfaces each idle item's producer-review state and a log tail,
recommends the idle panes to close, and closes them **only after my explicit
approval** — so finished dispatch panes stop accumulating and holding memory/CPU.

## Context

- Agents that end with `</end_session>` leave their pane open; these accumulate
  and hold memory (see WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS).
- Existing auto-close work (WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN, WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN) targets
  dispatch panes only and is already completed.
- This skill is the manual, workspace-scoped, approval-gated complement: it
  never closes anything unattended.

## Recommended source location

- **Canonical**: `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/` — `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a
  symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, so a global skill must live there.
- Assumption: tracked in ContextHub because the herdr pane lifecycle work lives
  here. Confirm whether the skill should instead be ContextHub-local
  (`.pi/skills/pane-triage/`). If ContextHub-local, it will not be globally
  available.

## Skill specification (fixed defaults, no execution-control flags)

**Name / description**

- `name: pane-triage`
- `disable-model-invocation: true`
- description: "Triage and clean up panes in the current herdr workspace: idle
  vs active, producer-review state, log tails, then close idle panes after
  explicit producer approval."

**Scope and terminology**

- Workspace = `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` of the invoking pane (fallback
  `herdr pane current`); the report covers only this workspace.
- Tabs via `herdr tab list --workspace <id>`; panes via
  `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`.
- Idle = the pane's `agent_session.value` file exists and its last non-empty
  JSONL entry is an assistant message whose concatenated `text` blocks
  (`.rstrip()`) end with `</end_session>`.
- Active = any other pane (including plain shells with no session).
- Needs Review = the idle pane's work item has `needsProducerReview == true`
  (`wl show <id> --json`). Work-item id parsed from the trailing
  ` - <PREFIX>-<HASH>` in the pane label.

**Fixed defaults**

- Workspace: invoking workspace only; no cross-workspace roll-up.
- Log tail: 20 lines of the final session message per idle item (no active logs).
- Close recommendation: always emitted.
- Closing: enabled (dry-run off) but only after explicit approval.
- Output: markdown to stdout, pasted verbatim by the invoking agent.

**Algorithm**

1. Resolve workspace and fetch its label/number; error clearly if outside herdr.
2. Enumerate tabs and panes; index panes by tab.
3. Derive `title = label || terminal_title || "(untitled)"`.
4. Classify each pane idle/active; build the Idle and Active tables.
5. Enrich idle panes with work item id and `needsProducerReview` (`n/a` if no id).
6. Print each idle pane's final-message tail under the heading
   `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
7. Emit the report.
8. Emit the "Recommended to close" table.
9. Ask for producer approval, then close.

**Report structure**

```
# Pane report — <workspace label> (<workspace id>)

## Idle
| Tab | Title | Pane ID | Work item | Needs Review |

## Active
| Tab | Title | Pane ID |

## Idle item logs
### <pane title> Needs Review <true|false>
```text
<last 20 lines of final session message>
```

## Recommended to close
| Title | Pane ID | Work item | Needs Review | Reason |

## Closed
| Pane ID | Result |
```

**Recommend-to-close rules**

- Idle panes → recommended.
- Idle with `needsProducerReview == true` → recommended, annotated `review-pending`.
- Active panes / plain shells → not recommended.
- The invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) → never recommended and never closed.

**Approval and closing**

- Mandatory blocking prompt: "N idle panes are recommended to close: <ids>.
  Close them? (yes / select / no)". `no`, or any ambiguity, closes nothing.
- `yes` → close all recommended; `select <ids>` → close only those.
- Immediately before closing, re-read `herdr pane list` and re-classify: drop
  any pane that is no longer idle, is the invoking pane, or no longer exists.
- Close with `herdr pane close <pane_id>`, one at a time; continue on individual
  failure and report a per-pane ledger; non-zero exit if any close failed.
- Idempotent: already-closed panes are skipped.

**Safety contract**

- Never close the invoking pane, under any circumstances.
- No approval → no mutation.
- Never act on the earlier snapshot alone; re-verify before closing.
- Never close more panes than approved.
- No unattended/automatic closing.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `/skill:pane-triage` resolves the invoking workspace from
   `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` (fallback `herdr pane current`) and reports only it.
2. Idle classification requires the last non-empty session entry to be an
   assistant message ending with `</end_session>`; a marker quoted mid-message
   does not qualify.
3. The report renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle
   items, the work item id and `needsProducerReview` value.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading
   `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. A "Recommended to close" table lists idle panes and excludes the invoking
   pane; `needsProducerReview=true` rows are annotated `review-pending`.
6. No pane is closed without explicit producer approval (`yes`/`select`);
   `no`/ambiguity closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
7. Approved panes are re-verified idle immediately before closing; any pane that
   became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.
8. Offline fixture tests cover classification, marker-mid-message rejection,
   work-item id parsing, `needsProducerReview` mapping, recommendation rules,
   and approval gating (no approval → zero close calls).

## References

- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not
  closed on completion (evaluated for deferral to this skill).
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch
  panes, except implement.
- WL-0MU4US5MP001JFEN — implement auto-close logic with implement exception.

## Goal

As a herdr operator, I want a minimum cooldown between successive downtime
dispatches of the same work item after a pane ends **without reaching a
terminal stage**, so a repeatedly failing session cannot be re-selected
immediately and waste local-LLM slots.

## Problem Statement

During the 3-hour window examined on 2026-09-28 (05:02–08:02 local), the
downtime dispatcher recorded 6 non-scheduled dispatches. 5 of the
corresponding panes closed with a non-terminal reason code
(`agent-ended-no-terminal` x4, `audit-ended-no-result` x1):

| Item | Kind | Close reason |
|------|------|--------------|
| `WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K` | plan | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUBVH9FV0027COG` | intake | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2` | intake | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUH765F1003FKRK` | intake | `agent-ended-no-terminal` |
| `WL-0MUKH3DVA00488U0` | audit | `audit-ended-no-result` |

Re-eligibility of an item after such a close is currently governed only by
the dispatched success-marker TTL (`DEFAULT_DOWNTIME_MARKER_STALE_WINDOW_MS`,
24 h) and the stage-advancement guard. There is **no explicit minimum-dwell
cooldown** keyed on the outcome of the previous dispatch, so the policy for
"how soon may we try this item again after it failed" is implicit and
depends entirely on the coarse 24 h marker window. A shorter, deliberate
cooldown is needed so a failed session does not immediately consume another
slot when the marker window is shortened, reset, or bypassed (e.g. critical
escalation, marker-loss, or a stage transition caused by a partial run).

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** runs the downtime dispatcher and expects failed
  sessions not to be retried in a tight loop.
- **Pi agent (AI):** receives auto-dispatches; should not receive the same
  item again until the cooldown elapses.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Cooldown on non-terminal close:** When a downtime pane for an
   item closes with a non-terminal reason code (`agent-ended-no-terminal`,
   `audit-ended-no-result`, or any future non-terminal code), that item is
   excluded from re-dispatch of the **same kind** until at least
   `cooldownMs` has elapsed since the close timestamp.
2. **AC2 — Configurable + clamped:** The cooldown is read from settings
   (`downtimeNonTerminalCooldownMs` or equivalent), re-read fresh each tick,
   with a defensive floor (no immediate retry) and a ceiling (cannot strand
   an item indefinitely). Document the defaults and clamps.
3. **AC3 — Neutral, never a strike:** The cooldown is a neutral skip (like
   `code-freeze` / `audit-in-flight`) — it must NOT count towards the
   three-strike CLI-error rule and must NOT trigger the no-candidate
   cooldown when it is the only reason a candidate was skipped; the terminal
   reason must be distinguishable from `no-candidate`.
4. **AC4 — Stage advancement releases:** If the item advances past its
   dispatched-at stage, the cooldown is released immediately (a genuinely
   progressed item is not held back).
5. **AC5 — Terminal success unaffected:** A successful terminal close
   (e.g. `closed-as-intake-complete`, `closed-as-plan-complete`,
   `reached-in-review`) does not apply the non-terminal cooldown.
6. **AC6 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: (a) non-terminal close then immediate
   idle cycle → skipped with the cooldown reason; (b) close older than
   `cooldownMs` → eligible; (c) stage advancement mid-cooldown → eligible;
   (d) terminal success → eligible per existing semantics; (e) missing /
   unparseable close timestamp → fail-closed skip.
7. **AC7 — Both dispatch paths:** The control applies to BOTH the
   Herdr-list-head path (`dispatchFromHerdrList`) and the coordination
   offer path (`dispatchFromCoordination` / `computeMostImportantItem`).

## Constraints

- TypeScript under `packages/herdr/src/`; reuse the existing rolling dispatch
  log (`downtime-log.ts`) as the source of pane-close outcomes.
- Fail-closed default: if the close outcome cannot be read, prefer the safe
  (no-dispatch) behaviour.
- No second ranking implementation on the dispatch path — this is a
  sequential **filter**, matching the existing gate pipeline.

## Existing State

- Dispatched-marker readers already in `downtime-log.ts`
  (`dispatchedItemMarkers`, `markerStillExcludes`).
- Pane-lifecycle close entries already carry `reasonCode`
  (`pane-lifecycle.ts`, `downtime-log.ts`).
- Gate pipeline documented in `downtime-worker.ts` module header.

data.description:
## Goal

As a herdr operator, I want a per-item cap on the number of automatic
downtime dispatch attempts (per skill/kind), so a work item that keeps
failing to reach a terminal stage is surfaced for human attention instead of
being dispatched indefinitely.

## Problem Statement

The downtime dispatcher has no per-item attempt budget. Re-dispatch is bounded
only by the success-marker TTL and the stage-advancement guard. Repeated
non-terminal closes (observed as `agent-ended-no-terminal` /
`audit-ended-no-result` during the 2026-09-28 review window) can therefore
consume local-LLM slots across many idle cycles without any escalation. There
is no machine-readable count of how many times the dispatcher has attempted
an item, and no threshold at which the item is flagged for producer review.

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** wants failing items to stop consuming dispatch slots and
  to be visible for manual triage.
- **Producer/reviewer:** wants a flag on items that have exhausted their
  automatic dispatch budget.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Attempt counter:** The dispatcher derives (from the rolling
   dispatch log) the per-item, per-kind count of dispatch attempts, including
   attempts whose pane closed non-terminally. No new persistent store is
   required if the existing log suffices; if a dedicated counter is needed,
   it must be derived/fail-open-readable.
2. **AC2 — Cap enforced:** Once the count reaches `maxAttempts` (configurable,
   clamped to a sane range, default documented), the item is excluded from
   further automatic dispatch of that kind.
3. **AC3 — Escalation:** On reaching the cap, the item is flagged
   `needsProducerReview = true` (and/or recorded with a distinct reason such
   as `attempt-budget-exhausted`) so it surfaces for human triage rather than
   silently looping.
4. **AC4 — Stage advancement resets:** A stage advancement clears the
   budget for the previous kind (the item has demonstrably progressed).
5. **AC5 — Neutral skip reason:** A budget-exhausted skip is a neutral reason,
   distinct from `no-candidate`, and never counts as a CLI-error strike.
6. **AC6 — Both dispatch paths:** The cap applies to BOTH the
   Herdr-list-head path and the coordination offer path.
7. **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: (a) count below cap → eligible;
   (b) count at cap → skipped with `attempt-budget-exhausted`; (c) flag set
   exactly once; (d) stage advancement resets the count; (e) corrupt/missing
   log → fail-open count of 0 (never block all dispatch).

## Constraints

- TypeScript under `packages/herdr/src/`.
- Must not weaken the existing duplicate-dispatch protections
  (`WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4`, `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT`) — additive only.
- The cap is a sequential **filter** on the ranked candidate sequence, not a
  new ranking.

## Existing State

- Rolling dispatch log and marker readers in `downtime-log.ts`.
- `needsProducerReview` is already honoured as a global exclusion by the
  dispatcher, so setting it is sufficient to stop re-dispatch once flagged.

discovered-from:SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 (SorraAgents worklog)

## Goal

The producer (SorraAgents work item SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2, epic SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ)
asked for a ContextHub work item that investigates **why** a raised host-wide
test-concurrency cap (`TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) was believed present in the
downtime/herdr harness, and that agrees an alternative approach with the agent;
the offending override is then to be removed.

## Producer decision (2026-09-28)

1. Raise a work item here to investigate why the override is present and agree an
   alternative with the agent.
2. Remove it.

## Investigation result (evidence)

**No `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` override exists in the ContextHub/herdr harness.**

- `git log --all -S "TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY"` in ContextHub returns **no commits** —
  the string has never existed on any branch (source, `dist`, or config).
- No occurrence in `packages/herdr` source or `packages/herdr/dist`, the shipped
  `herdr` binary (`grep -a`), `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`,
  `~/.config/herdr/plugins*`, `~/.herdr/downtime/*`, or any shell dotfile.
- No occurrence in the environments of the herdr server, the `run-pi-agent.sh`
  wrappers, or the dispatched pi agents (checked `/proc/<pid>/environ`).
- The audit debug log from the incident
  (`~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/green_suite_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T111823.log`)
  records the actual value at the time:
  `test concurrency slot busy: no free slot within 600s (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2)`
  — the default, **not** a raised cap.
- `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (separate `"audit"` namespace, default 1) does appear in
  ContextHub history, but it is unrelated to the `"test"` namespace.

## Actual cause of the observed oversubscription

The apparent "~8 concurrent suites" was **not** a harness env override. It was:

1. **Unpaced call paths** that call `run_cached()` directly instead of the test
   skill's semaphore-guarded `run_tests.py`: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
   (route fixed by SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG) and the audit F3 auto-execution path
   (SA-0MUJK94QN0015925). Those executions bypass the host-wide `"test"` semaphore.
2. **Stale semaphore slot files** `/run/user/1000/pi-semaphores/test/2..9`.
   `Semaphore._ensure_slots` only ever *adds* slots (up to `max_workers`) and never
   prunes extras. The extras are inert for a process with `max_workers=2` (its
   `_try_acquire_slot` iterates `range(max_workers)`), but they misled diagnosis and
   were cited as evidence of an 8-slot ceiling.

## Proposed alternatives (to agree with the agent)

1. **No harness-level `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` override** — none exists today; keep the
   test skill's env-var + default-2 as the single source of truth.
2. **Prune stale slots in `Semaphore._ensure_slots`** (SorraAgents
   `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) so the on-disk slot count converges to
   `max_workers`, removing the misleading residue.
3. **Close the unpaced call paths** (owned by the SorraAgents children named above)
   so every real suite execution acquires the host-wide `"test"` semaphore.
4. **Optional dispatcher deferral** — treat host-wide test saturation as a reason to
   defer test/implement dispatch, analogous to the existing audit-slot dispatch gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Recorded, with evidence, whether any harness/herd code sets `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY`;
      if none, close the item with that finding and no harness code change.
- [ ] An agreed alternative documented (env-only, prune stale slots, close unpaced paths,
      optional dispatcher deferral).
- [ ] If pruning/coordination is agreed, a test proves the on-disk slot count converges
      to `max_workers` after a higher-`max_workers` run.
- [ ] Cross-references SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ and SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 (SorraAgents).

## Interim action taken

The stale test-namespace slot files `2..9` (unused by any `max_workers=2` process;
slots `0..1` were held by live suites) were removed on 2026-09-28 as the concrete
raised-capacity artefact. This is a one-off cleanup; the durable fix is AC2 (pruning).

## Related

- SA-0MUJL211C008GHMZ — Implement test job pacing to prevent resource oversubscription (epic)
- SA-0MUA8BSAG000YZA2 — Browser suite contention: TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2 starvation
- SA-0MUKHCO02009EQFG — Route implement.py test execution through the test skill pacer
- SA-0MUJK94QN0015925 — audit F3 auto-execution bypasses the test concurrency semaphore

# Log projection helper: recentDispatchedItems

**Parent:** WL-0MUGLL9SS002E1D2 (Recent dispatches summary)

## Goal

Add a projection function to `downtime-log.ts` that reads the rolling dispatch log via the existing fail-safe reader and returns the up-to-20 most recent dispatched work items, deduplicated by id and ordered newest-first.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New exported function `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit?)` reads via the existing fail-safe `readDowntimeLogEntries(cwd)`; a missing/unreadable/empty/malformed log yields `[]` with no throw.
- Non-dispatch-marker entries (pane-close/lifecycle entries with `entryType: 'pane-close'`) are ignored by the projection.
- Rows are deduplicated by work item id — one row per id — using that item's most recent log entry for ordering and metadata.
- Rows are ordered by their most recent log-entry timestamp, newest first.
- The result is capped at 20 rows (configurable via `limit`, default 20).
- Each row is a `RecentDispatchRow` carrying at least: `itemId`, `title`, `kind`, `latestOutcome` (when a pane-close entry exists), and `latestTimestamp`.
- A missing/empty title falls back to a placeholder (e.g. `[unknown]`) rather than a blank row; malformed JSONL lines are skipped without throwing.
- Unit tests cover: dedup by id, newest-first ordering, 20-row cap, kind/outcome mapping, missing title, malformed lines, and the empty/missing-log fail-safe path.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Define exported interface `RecentDispatchRow` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`.
2. Implement `recentDispatchedItems(cwd, limit = 20)` reading entries and reducing into a `Map<itemId, RecentDispatchRow>` keyed by id (last-write-wins on the newest entry).
3. Sort by latest timestamp descending, slice to `limit`.
4. Add unit tests to `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts` (test-first: write the projection tests before the helper body).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- None.
